why: loc_mq304_ce_2 is a small container yard in Dogtown's Longshore Stacks: stacked containers, two guard areas, and two security-area controllers. mq304 uses it for an ambient city encounter in which three scavengers squat on routine spots (one taking drugs, one on a phone), two Barghest grunts arrive on guard-stand spots, and one scavenger opens fire on them. The ground is permanent world streaming, so the yard stays. This proposal restores its normal life as a scavenger squat: the three scavengers on their calm routine workspots, with the quest's Barghest pair, attitude overrides, shoot-at node and security transitions left out.

open_questions: Check the yard has a calm scav camp. Stand in the container yard: three scavengers should be idle on routine spots (one on a phone, one taking drugs, one standing), not crouched, aiming or fighting.

Check the scavengers actually appear in the yard. Their community has no area node in the converted sectors, so confirm all three spawn inside this yard (not floating, inside a container or a block away) and are not T-posing.
Check the yard is not a restricted area. Walk across the whole yard: no trespass banner or Barghest warning should appear; both vanilla security areas are DISABLED and must stay so.
Check the anchor flips on approach. Walk toward the yard and confirm the tour breadcrumb _prox turns on; the wait is on the scav side's security-area controller at the yard's north edge.
Check nothing of the quest scene is left. There should be no second Barghest pair, no quest cars, no shootout, no invisible encounter trigger and no lingering combat music or attitude change.
Check the yard does not double-populate. If the combat zone's own ambient encounters also spawn scavs or Barghest inside this prefab, report the overlap so the camp can be dropped.

communities.why: Phase a is the community's only phase (its initial state) and the scene sends scav_1 to a calm routine spot, #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_01_b, which plays stand-ground-phone-talk: a scavenger hanging around the yard, not a combat pose. Scavengers are one of Longshore Stacks' two listed gangs, so a small squat here is the neighbourhood's normal life. No community area node maps the entry to a spot in any converted sector, so the tour must confirm where he stands.

Phase a; the scene places scav_2 on #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_02_b (routine stand_ground), and the community's own un-suffixed spot #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_02 plays routine__drug__stand_ground_drug__take. Both are idle squat poses. Same missing area mapping as scav_1.

Phase a; the scene places scav_3 on #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_03_b (routine stand_ground), and the community's own spot #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_03 plays routine__stand_ground. Three scavengers on routine spots read as a squat, not a firing line. Same missing area mapping as scav_1.

deferred_prefab_owner: world streaming (the chosen people need no quest prefab)

tour_stop.source: mean of worldAISpotNode #ep1_mq304_ce_2_scav_01, _02, _03 in base/worlds/03_night_city/_compiled/default/ep1/exterior_-20_-22_0_1.streamingsector (the yard's own scav spot group; the scene's alternate _b group is about 28 m west in exterior_-40_-44_0_0)

proximity_wait.why: The venue is open ground with no door, lift or terminal; its only device entities are the two scav and two Barghest security-area controllers in its own devices prefab. #mq304_ce_2_scavs_sec_area is a worldDeviceNode at (-2488.60,-2761.83,28.51) in the always-streamed sector exterior_-39_-44_0_0, about 11 m from the scene's scav workspots and 19 m from the scav group's own spots, so a distance pause on it resolves inside the yard. Its SecurityAreaControllerPS has securityAreaType DISABLED, so waiting on it does not put the player in a trespass area.
